title: Initial evaluation, low back after lifting

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Tomas. Let's talk about your low back. I'll ask some questions first, then do a short exam.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay. It started six weeks ago when I lifted a drywall sheet. Pain is 6/10 at its worst, usually around 3 or 4.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Sitting longer than 30 minutes, and bending to put on socks. Standing helps.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I can't sleep on my left side anymore.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any pain or tingling going down either leg?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Some tingling in my right foot now and then, not constant. No fever, no bladder problems.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Have you lost weight without trying, or had night pain that wakes you up?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No weight loss. The pain wakes me once a night when I turn over.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: I didn't test strength today. We'll do that next visit.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My goal is to put on my own socks without pain, and get back to lifting boxes at my job.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Assessment: the pain started with a lifting strain. Forward bending is limited. Plan: start a short walking program and the two positions we went over, and I'll see you in one week.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Let's go over the positions now.

expectedFacts.statement: Sitting longer than 30 minutes makes it worse
Pain wakes the patient once a night
Goal: put on own socks without pain
Pain started with a lifting strain
